cities.base: Prawirotaman, south of the Kraton: quiet lanes, the best small hotels, ViaVia and Warung Bu Ageng on foot, and the Kraton and Taman Sari a fifteen minute walk. Malioboro is louder and worse value.
cities.name: Yogyakarta

cities.base: You do not need to sleep here unless you are doing the 04:00 sunrise entry, in which case Manohara is on the grounds. Otherwise a driver from Yogyakarta, ninety minutes each way, and the whole plain i
cities.name: Borobudur and the Magelang plain

cities.base: Cemoro Lawang, the village on the caldera rim at 2,200m: the rooms are basic and cold but you can walk to the rim and the jeeps leave from your door at 03:00. Do not sleep in Probolinggo or Malang.
cities.name: Bromo (Cemoro Lawang)

cities.base: Banyuwangi town or Licin on the road up: an hour to Paltuding for the 01:00 pickup, and the town has the nasi tempong and rujak soto. The Bondowoso side (Sempol) is closer but has almost nothing else.
cities.name: Banyuwangi (Ijen)

cities.base: The harbour end of Jalan Soekarno Hatta, within a walk of the jetty for 05:30 boat departures and of the Kampung Ujung seafood stalls. The resort hills to the north need a scooter for everything.
cities.name: Labuan Bajo

cities.base: Nobody sleeps on the islands; you either day-trip by speedboat from Labuan Bajo or sleep on a boat. A 3D2N liveaboard is the way to see Padar at sunrise without a hundred other people.
cities.name: Komodo National Park

places.name: Kraton Yogyakarta (Kedhaton)
places.note: The pavilions are plain but the court performance at 09:00 to 11:00 is included, gamelan on Tuesday, wayang kulit on Thursday, dance drama on Saturday.

places.name: Taman Sari water castle
places.note: The bathing pools are small and full of phones by 10:00; the underground Sumur Gumuling mosque and the kampung alleys behind it are the reason to come.

places.name: Kotagede old quarter walk
places.note: Start at Pasar Legi at 07:00, walk the joglo houses and the walled Mataram mosque and graves, and buy silver from a workshop rather than the showroom on the main road.

places.name: Pasar Beringharjo and Malioboro
places.note: The batik floor is the real thing at a third of shop prices and the sate kere and pecel stalls on the east side feed you for a dollar; Malioboro itself is a pedestrian mall you walk once.

places.name: Prambanan
places.note: Three Hindu towers taller than Borobudur with the Ramayana carved round the Shiva shrine; the last entry is 16:00, and the tour groups go after Candi Sewu at the far end of the grounds, so walk there.

places.name: Ratu Boko sunset
places.note: A gate on a hill and a few foundations, sold as a sunset for the same foreigner price as Prambanan; the view is fine and the site is not worth twenty dollars.

places.name: Ramayana Ballet at Prambanan
places.note: Two hours of Javanese dance with the lit temple behind the open-air stage, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, May to October; cheap seats are fine, the point is the backdrop.

places.name: Gudeg Yu Djum, Wijilan
places.note: The dry, sweet style of jackfruit gudeg with krecek and a whole egg; order it 'komplit' and eat it at the original on the gudeg street east of the Kraton.

places.name: Gudeg Pawon
places.note: They serve straight from the wood-fired kitchen from 22:00 and the pots are empty by midnight, so be in the queue at 21:45.

places.name: Sate Klathak Pak Pong
places.note: Young goat grilled on bicycle spokes with only salt, served with a bowl of clear goat broth; thirty minutes by ride-hail and the weekend dinner queue is real.

places.name: Mangut Lele Mbah Marto
places.note: Smoked catfish in a coconut chili gravy in a village house; you walk through to the kitchen, lift the lids and serve yourself, and it is gone by mid afternoon.

places.name: Angkringan Kopi Joss Lik Man
places.note: A lump of red-hot charcoal dropped into your coffee, nasi kucing parcels and sate from the cart, sitting on mats on the pavement with students until late.

places.name: Borobudur structure climb
places.note: Sessions of 150 people from 08:30 to 15:30 with mandatory Upanat sandals and a guide, about IDR 455,000 for foreigners; book the first session online, the grounds-only ticket does not get you on the terraces.

places.name: Borobudur sunrise from Manohara
places.note: The 04:00 entry with a torch and breakfast, capped at 100 people, about IDR 1,000,000; expensive, and the only way to be on top in the mist without a crowd.

places.name: Punthuk Setumbu
places.note: The hill everyone photographs Borobudur in the mist from, a 15 minute walk up from the car park; the temple is a small grey shape and the mist is a dry season thing.

places.name: Gereja Ayam (Bukit Rhema)
places.note: A concrete prayer house shaped like a chicken made famous by a film; the view from the crown is the same as Punthuk Setumbu next door and the inside is a gift shop.

places.name: Candi Mendut
places.note: A single chamber with a three metre seated Buddha that is better preserved than anything at Borobudur, and the Buddhist monastery next door lets you walk the garden.

places.name: Candi Pawon
places.note: The small third temple on the straight line from Mendut to Borobudur, in a village yard; ten minutes, and worth it only because you are passing.

places.name: Candi Selogriyo and the rice terraces
places.note: A 20 minute walk on a farm track through terraces on the flank of Sumbing to a small Hindu temple with nobody at it; an hour's drive from Borobudur and the reason to hire a car for the day.

places.name: Candirejo village by andong
places.note: A horse cart through tobacco and papaya fields to a tofu maker and the Progo river, run by the village cooperative; slow, and it shows you where the temple's stone came from.

places.name: Kupat Tahu Pojok, Magelang
places.note: Rice cakes, fried tofu and cabbage in a sweet peanut and garlic sauce at the corner stall Magelang has eaten at since the 1940s; pair it with Selogriyo on the way back.

places.name: Sop Senerek Bu Atmo, Magelang
places.note: Red bean and beef soup with spinach that Magelang eats for breakfast, a Dutch army leftover turned Javanese; the pot runs out by early afternoon.

places.name: Svarga Bumi
places.note: A rice paddy fitted with swings, frames and platforms for photos; the paddy across the road is free and does not have a ticket booth.

places.name: Penanjakan 1 sunrise viewpoint
places.note: The classic shot of Bromo, Batok and Semeru over the caldera, from a concrete platform with several hundred people; be on the rail by 04:00 or you photograph the backs of heads, and bring a real jacket, it is 5 degrees.

places.name: King Kong Hill
places.note: A dirt ledge on the road below Penanjakan with nearly the same angle and a tenth of the people; ask the jeep driver to stop here instead of going to the top.

places.name: Seruni Point
places.note: Lower and closer to Bromo than Penanjakan, with a new stepped platform, reachable in 45 minutes on foot from Cemoro Lawang; the volcano fills the frame but Semeru sits lower behind it.

places.name: Bromo crater rim
places.note: A 2km walk across the sand from the jeep park and 250 concrete steps to a rim with a rusted rail and the crater roaring below; it closes without notice when the gas alert rises, and the steps are a crush between 06:30 and 08:00.

places.name: Pura Luhur Poten
places.note: The Tengger Hindu temple on the sand at the foot of Bromo, closed to visitors except at Kasada when the community throws offerings into the crater; walk round it rather than through it.

places.name: Pasir Berbisik (whispering sands)
places.note: The open flat of black sand east of the crater where the jeeps stop for photos on the way to the savanna; five minutes of wind and ash and a good look back at Batok.

places.name: Savana (Bukit Teletubbies)
places.note: Green rolling grass on the south side of the caldera, brown by August; the jeeps all stop at the same spot, so walk 200m up the slope to lose them.

places.name: Bukit Mentigen walk from Cemoro Lawang
places.note: A 30 minute walk up from the village to a knoll on the rim with Bromo and Batok straight in front; the no-jeep sunrise, and just as good in the late afternoon when the jeeps have gone.

places.name: Madakaripura waterfall
places.note: A 20 minute walk up a river gorge to a 200m curtain of water in a stone chimney; you will be soaked, the rock falls after rain, and it fits on the way down to Probolinggo after the sunrise.

places.name: Cafe Lava
places.note: The hostel restaurant everyone ends up in for nasi goreng, soup and hot ginger by the fire; the food is plain and the alternative is a warung with the same menu and no fire.

places.name: Lava View Lodge terrace
places.note: The only terrace in the village that sits on the caldera edge, so a coffee here at 16:00 is the afternoon view of Bromo with the sand emptying out.

places.name: Tengger pony ride to the crater steps
places.note: A man leads a small horse 1.5km across flat sand you can walk in 25 minutes; pay for it only if you cannot manage the walk, and haggle.

places.name: Kawah Ijen crater rim
places.note: 3km and 500m up a wide track from Paltuding, two hours in the dark, to a rim over the largest acid lake on earth, turquoise once the sun is on it; foreigner ticket about IDR 100,000 weekdays and 150,000 weekends, booked online, plus a health certificate from the post at the gate.

places.name: Blue fire, Ijen crater floor
places.note: A 30 minute scramble down loose rock in the dark with a rented gas mask to burning sulphur gas at the vents; the flames are small and blue-ish rather than the photos, the descent is closed on high gas nights, and you must be back up before it gets light.

places.name: Ijen trolley (taxi cart)
places.note: Three men pull you up the track in a wooden cart for around IDR 800,000 to 1,200,000 return; it exists because the miners lost the sulphur income, but if you can walk, walk.

places.name: Kawah Wurung
places.note: A grassed-over crater bowl 40 minutes beyond Paltuding on the plateau road, with a short walk to the rim and cattle in it; the thing to do at 08:00 after Ijen when you are too awake to sleep.

places.name: Kalibendo plantation
places.note: A Dutch-era rubber, coffee and clove estate on the road up to Ijen with a river to swim in and a shed selling the coffee; a stop on the way back down rather than a destination.

places.name: Air Terjun Jagir
places.note: Twin falls into a swimming pool ten minutes' walk from the road; a local Sunday spot, small, and a good swim after the Ijen morning.

places.name: Kemiren Osing village and Sanggar Genjah Arum
places.note: The village of the Osing, the pre-Islamic Javanese of Banyuwangi, and a coffee house of old wooden houses where the owner roasts Osing coffee and gamelan groups rehearse; call ahead, it is not a walk-in cafe.

places.name: Baluran, Bekol savanna and Bama beach
places.note: A 12km track in through teak to a dry savanna with deer, banteng, peacocks and Baluran volcano behind, then mangroves and a swim at Bama; go at gate opening, by 10:00 the animals are in the shade.

places.name: Nasi Tempong Mbok Wah
places.note: Banyuwangi's dish: rice, boiled greens, fried fish or chicken and a raw chili sambal that slaps (tempong) you, at the house everybody names first.

places.name: Pondok Rujak Soto
places.note: Peanut-sauce vegetable rujak with beef soto ladled over it, which sounds wrong and is the town's signature; a plate with iced tea is about IDR 23,000.

places.name: Rumah Makan Pecel Ayu
places.note: Pecel rawon, the other Banyuwangi hybrid: peanut vegetable salad drowned in black keluak beef rawon, at the place the town sends visiting officials.

places.name: Sego Cawuk Bu Mantih
places.note: Rice with grated young coconut and corn in a sour, spicy broth eaten for breakfast, only in the morning and only worth it on the way to or from the airport, which is nearby.

places.name: Puncak Waringin
places.note: A terraced viewpoint five minutes above the main street, built for the 2023 summit, looking over the harbour and the islands at sunset; free and the easiest sundown in town.

places.name: Bukit Sylvia
places.note: A 15 minute walk up a dry hill for a 360 view of the bay and the islands going orange; take a scooter, be up by 17:15, and expect drone noise at weekends.

places.name: Bukit Amelia Sea View
places.note: The next hill along from Sylvia with a lower, quieter platform over the same water; pick one, not both.

places.name: Goa Batu Cermin
places.note: A short limestone cave with fossil coral in the roof and a shaft of light around noon; fine for a rainy hour, sold as more than it is.

places.name: Goa Rangko
places.note: 40 minutes by road then a 15 minute fishing boat, around IDR 300,000 to 500,000 for the boat, to a cave with a clear saltwater pool you swim in; the light comes through the roof between 12:00 and 14:00 and that is the only time to go.

places.name: Cunca Wulang
places.note: An hour and a half on a mountain road then 40 minutes down through forest to a narrow canyon where you jump off rock ledges into deep green water with a village guide; a half day, and a hot climb back.

places.name: Melo village caci whip fight
places.note: The Manggarai men's whip and shield duel with gongs and drums, staged for visitors by the village on request; it is a booking, not a drop-in, and it is real fighting, they draw blood.

places.name: Kampung Ujung night seafood stalls
places.note: A row of plastic-table stalls on the waterfront where you pick a snapper or squid off the ice and it comes grilled with sambal and rice; cash only, agree the price per kilo before it goes on the fire.

places.name: Tree Top
places.note: A wooden deck over the main street with the harbour sunset and grilled fish and Indonesian plates for IDR 30,000 to 100,000; locally run, and the sunset table needs you there by 17:30.

places.name: Paradise Bar
places.note: A reggae bar on the hill with live bands most nights and Bintang over the bay; the one place in town that is open late, and a small cover on Saturdays.
places.neighborhood: Binongko hill, north end of town

places.name: Cafe.in.hit
places.note: Flores coffee and a proper breakfast from 06:30, which matters on a town where boats leave at 05:30 and most kitchens open at 08:00.

places.name: Padar island viewpoint
places.note: About 800 steps and 150m up to the ridge over three bays of different coloured sand, the photo of the whole park; there is a daily cap and a ranger fee, three sessions a day, and only the sunrise slot from a boat anchored overnight is quiet.

places.name: Pink Beach (Pantai Merah)
places.note: Sand tinted by red coral fragments, pinker in the wet line than in the photos, with a good shallow reef straight off the beach; stay near the boat, dragons walk this beach.

places.name: Loh Liang, Komodo island dragon trek
places.note: A ranger with a forked stick walks a group of up to five on a short or medium loop from the ranger station; the dragons are usually near the kitchen, the park entry is IDR 150,000 weekdays and 250,000 weekends for foreigners plus the ranger fee, and the day quota is registered through the boat opera

places.name: Loh Buaya, Rinca dragon trek
places.note: Closer than Komodo, drier, with more dragons per walk and a raised concrete boardwalk built in 2022 that keeps you above them; the better bet for actually seeing dragons, the worse for feeling like a wild island.

places.name: Manta Point (Karang Makassar)
places.note: A long shallow reef with a current where reef mantas feed most days of the year; you jump in from the boat, drift, get picked up, and repeat, and the snorkel permit is extra.
places.neighborhood: Makassar reef, between Komodo and Padar

places.name: Taka Makassar sandbar
places.note: A crescent of white sand a few metres wide in turquoise water, gone at high tide; twenty minutes of wading and a photo, nothing more, and every day boat stops.

places.name: Kanawa island
places.note: A small island with a long jetty, a reef with turtles and a 15 minute hill walk, half an hour by speedboat; the last stop on most day trips and a fair one.

places.name: Kelor island
places.note: A steep 15 minute scramble to a small summit over two beaches, and a reef off the front; the closest island to town and the fallback when the sea is too rough for Padar.

places.name: Pulau Kalong bats at dusk
places.note: Thousands of fruit bats leave the mangroves at sunset and stream over the boat towards Flores for ten minutes; only liveaboards are out here at that hour.

places.name: Gili Lawa Darat
places.note: A 30 minute hill climb to a ridge over a lagoon that outdoes Padar with a tenth of the people, but it is in the north where only two or three night boats go.

places.name: Batu Bolong
places.note: A rock the size of a car above water and a wall of coral and fish below it, the best snorkel or dive in the park; the current rips on the wrong tide and boats only stop at slack.

places.name: Siaba Besar turtle bay
places.note: A sheltered bay with seagrass where green turtles graze in three metres of water; calm, easy, and the stop the boat makes when Manta Point is empty.

outings.why: The only way to be on the top terraces in the dark and see the stupas come out of the mist; capped at 100 people a day and booked out weeks ahead in July and August, and from Yogyakarta the car leaves at 02:45.
outings.name: Borobudur sunrise (Manohara 04:00 entry)
outings.season: All year; May to September for clear mornings
outings.fallback: Punthuk Setumbu hill at 04:30 for the same mist view from outside, then a regular 08:30 structure session

outings.why: Structure tickets run in sessions of 150 from 08:30 to 15:30 with mandatory sandals and a guide, so book the first session online the day before; Mendut and Pawon are on the same axis and take an hour together.
outings.name: Borobudur structure climb, Mendut and Pawon
outings.fallback: Grounds only plus Mendut if the sessions are full

outings.why: Leave at 15:00 for the low light on the Shiva tower, walk out to Candi Sewu at the north end which most people skip, then the open-air ballet at 19:30 on Tuesday, Thursday or Saturday from May to October.
outings.name: Prambanan and the Ramayana ballet
outings.season: Ballet open-air May to October; indoor stage the rest of the
outings.fallback: Prambanan only, two hours, any day

outings.why: A 60m rope descent into a sinkhole and a walk through to the Grubug chamber where the light shaft comes in between 10:00 and 12:00; numbers are limited daily and it is 90 minutes each way on bad roads.
outings.name: Jomblang cave
outings.season: All year; muddy November to March
outings.fallback: Merapi lava jeep tour from Kaliurang, four hours

outings.why: Jeep at 03:00, Penanjakan 1 by 04:00 for a spot on the rail, sunrise around 05:15, then down across the sand to the 250 steps to the crater rim and back by 09:00; the park ticket must be bought online at least a day ahead.
outings.name: Penanjakan sunrise and the Bromo crater
outings.season: All year; the park closes for Nyepi in March, for Kasada in
outings.fallback: Walk from Cemoro Lawang to Bukit Mentigen for the same sunrise without a jeep, then walk the sand to the crater, five hours on foot

outings.why: Pickup 00:30 to 01:00, gate opens 02:00, 3km and 500m of climb on a wide track to the rim by 04:00, then 30 minutes down into the crater with a gas mask if the ranger allows it; the flames are weaker than the photos and some nights are shut
outings.name: Kawah Ijen and the blue fire
outings.season: All year; closed the first Friday of each month for cleaning
outings.fallback: Start at 04:00 for sunrise on the rim only, no crater descent, with the lake turquoise by 06:00

outings.why: Ninety minutes north to a dry savanna with deer, banteng and peacocks at dawn and Bama beach at the end of the track; go at first light or it is empty and hot.
outings.name: Baluran, the Bekol savanna
outings.season: June to October for the dry yellow grass; green and quieter
outings.fallback: Jagir waterfall and Kemiren village, three hours

outings.why: Speedboat at 05:30, Padar at 07:30 when the light and the crowds are both at their worst, dragons at Loh Liang with a ranger, then the mantas and back by 17:30; it is long and it is the whole park in one go, which is why most people do the
outings.name: Komodo day boat: Padar, Pink Beach, Loh Liang, Manta Point
outings.season: April to November; December to February the sea gets rough a
outings.fallback: Rinca (Loh Buaya) and Kelor island, six hours, when the west is too rough

destination.name: Java and Komodo
destination.pitch: Two of the best temples in Asia, two volcanoes you climb in the dark, and dragons at the end, held together by three internal flights and a lot of 2am alarms.
destination.caveat: Three internal flights and two 2am departures in twelve days means you arrive in Flores tired, and the Komodo park quota can sell out weeks ahead in July and August. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Yogyakarta is a real city with students, batik and wayang, but the others are one-street towns you sleep in on the way to something.
because.food: Yogyakarta is the best eating city in Indonesia: gudeg from the kitchen at midnight, goat sate on bicycle spokes, smoked catfish in a village shed, all for under five dollars.
because.nature: Bromo's sea of sand at dawn, the acid lake at Ijen, and manta rays under the boat at Karang Makassar are three landscapes that do not look like anywhere else.
because.culture: Borobudur and Prambanan are a ninth century Buddhist and Hindu pair fifty kilometres apart, and the Kraton still runs daily court performances.
because.adventure: Two volcano climbs in the dark, a crater descent with a gas mask, and dragons on a trail with a ranger and a forked stick.
because.relaxation: Only the liveaboard deck qualifies, and only once you have done the sunrise climbs.
because.exploration: Every base is a real working town or village with a market, and nothing is set up for you the way Bali is.
